title: A refused token step is logged with the client id and the reason
purpose: On 10 October 2026 the haematite Studio door's sign-in was refused at Lys's token step. It had sent the app's API bearer as its client secret. Nobody could read why from Lys: the token handler (crates/lys-identity-server/src/provider/endpoints.rs `token`, about line 292) answers the refusal in OAuth's words through refusal::oauth_refusal, and writes nothing to the service's log. The reasons exist in Lys's own words: provider/client_auth.rs `authenticated` names `the app holds no live client credential`, `no approved app holds that client id`, `no live client credential of this app holds that secret`, the broker's refusal and SecretsUnavailable. But they reach only the product, which may not show them. Waffles carded it at 15:23: Lys writes one log line, with the client_id and the reason, on a refused token step. Building it (15:4x) found one more thing: the identity server installs no tracing subscriber (main.rs prints its log through the `say` sink, println to stdout, which the install keeps as identity.log), so every `tracing::warn!` in lys-identity-server reaches no one. The line therefore goes through `say`, as every other line the operator reads does.
task: On every refused token request, write one warn line to the identity server's log naming the client_id presented (from the Basic header or the form; `none` when neither names one), the OAuth error code answered, Lys's name for the refusal, and its reason. Never write the secret, the code, the verifier or the refresh token. Build the line in one function a test can call.

requirements.title: One log line per refused token request, naming the client and the reason
requirements.spec: Behavioural. WHEN /oauth/token answers a refusal, THE SYSTEM SHALL say exactly one line on the service's log, through the AppState `say` sink that every log line goes through: `token request refused: client_id <id> error <code> refusal <name> reason <reason>`. Here <id> is the client id the request presented in its Basic header or form, or `none`; <code> is the OAuth code oauth_refusal answers; <name> is Lys's error name; <reason> is the refusal's own words. The line SHALL NOT carry the client secret, the authorization code, the PKCE verifier, the refresh token or any credential value. A token request that succeeds SHALL say no such line.
acceptance: A function in provider/refusal.rs, `refused_fields(client_id: Option<&str>, error: &ServerError)`, answers the four fields as RefusedFields. A unit test gives it CredentialRefused{reason: "no live client credential of this app holds that secret"} with client_id Some("haematite"), and gets client_id haematite, error invalid_client, refusal credential_refused and that reason.
The same test gives ClientUnknown with client_id None and gets client_id `none`, error invalid_client.

A provider test (tests/shared/provider_client_credentials.rs) starts the service with Service::start_saying and keeps every line it says. It issues the fixture product a credential and signs in with it, and no `token request refused` line is said. It then presents that credential with a suffix, is answered 401, and finds exactly one `token request refused` line naming client_id fixture_product, invalid_client and credential_refused. Neither credential value appears in any line.

boundaries: The answer to the product is unchanged: the same status, OAuth code and body as today.
No secret, code, verifier, refresh token or credential value is ever written to the log; the reason strings are Lys's own and carry none.

No new dependency: the line goes through the existing `say` sink, and the test reads it through the harness's start_saying. Installing a tracing subscriber for the server's other warn events is a separate row, not this brief's.
verification: cargo clippy -p lys-identity-server --all-targets -- -D warnings and the provider tests; after the next Lys install, one refused curl to /oauth/token with client_id haematite and a wrong secret writes one `token request refused` line naming haematite in the identity log, read back with a token and secret filter.
